content:
Thursday, November 26th 2026
![Rockstar Games](https://tpucdn.com/images/news/rockstargames-v1795442328.png)
The IWGB has been working since early 2026 to establish the Rockstar Workers Union at Rockstar North in the UK, seeking negotiation for pay and bonuses, overtime, redundancies, flexible working arrangements, and generative AI policies. However, following a series of meetings, the would-be IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union held a recognition vote on November 26. According to a confirmation from the IWGB itself, that union vote did not succeed. Reportedly, the vote failed with 25% of employees voting for union recognition and 75% voting against recognition. According to Jason Schreier, Rockstar's head of publishing issued the following statement following the failed union vote:
We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together
The full statement from the IWGB Game Workers Union reads:
For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector, and a fairer society—this isn't a sign of retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favor of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognise we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We're ready to put in the effort to make that happen.
Whilst we haven't emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions will lead us.
A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy. But it's one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. We'll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against AI and layoffs.
The power to shape our working lives has always been, and will always be, in our hands.
